enquiry: We manufacture tablets from a powder blend containing an active pharmaceutical ingredient and excipients. Laboratory checks tell us whether the blend is on target, but results arrive after the material has moved through the press. We want to assess whether a fiber based measurement in the feed frame could follow API concentration changes. Our first pilot should compare reasonable measurement options before we commit to production equipment.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If single-method NIR diffuse reflection cannot resolve the API due to severe excipient band overlap, Raman or dual-method fusion would be evaluated.
proposal.next_step: Conduct laboratory feasibility trials with representative powder blend samples to test single-method NIR diffuse reflection against independent reference assays.

assessment.brief_answer: Fiber-based NIR diffuse reflection spectroscopy in the feed frame is recommended as the primary approach for tracking API concentration changes in powder blends. Non-contact NIR and Raman spectroscopy offer viable comparison options, with dual-method fusion available if single-method accuracy proves insufficient. Initial feasibility testing on representative blends with independent reference assays is recommended before pilot installation.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data from different sources into a new data matrix by placing the variables one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This approach could be tested to combine different spectral inputs for monitoring blend homogeneity, though one should evaluate dataset complementarity first as suggested in literature.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This review concept may not directly transfer from laboratory or general industrial setups to a specific powder feed frame without thorough validation.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
